_comment: Lane -> browser PROFILE, plus named destinations within a profile.
RESOLVED 2026-09-14. Both deviceIds were MEASURED, not inferred: each browser was
selected in turn and https://myaccount.google.com/ read for the signed-in address.
Neither was taken by elimination, because Arc/Brave/Chromium/Edge/Firefox are also
installed and a connected extension need not be one of the two Chrome profiles.
A Chrome WINDOW IS NOT A BROWSER IDENTITY. The Claude extension attaches per PROFILE,
so every window of a profile shares one deviceId -- and cookies are profile-wide, so
BYU library auth is already present in ANY window or tab of the personal profile.
There is NO third deviceId, and 'library' is a DESTINATION (a URL), not a role.
MECHANISM (Claude Code v2.1.259, read from the binary): the MCP prompts only when the
global pin (~/.claude.json .chromeExtension.pairedDeviceId) matches no connected browser.
A match auto-connects silently. requirePairedDevice is consumed but never provided by
SIDE EFFECT, MEASURED: select_browser REWRITES THE GLOBAL PIN. selectedDeviceId is
per-process so no RUNNING lane is disturbed, but the default every NEW session inherits
is left pointing at the browser that was borrowed. Any lane that borrows the non-default
profile must run `chrome-pin.sh restore` when it is done.

library.note: BYU HBLL. Auth is a PROFILE-WIDE cookie, so any window or tab of the personal profile has it. Open a new tab rather than hunting for Sir's window.
library.verified: 2026-09-14: navigated https://dbs.lib.byu.edu/jstor in Browser 1 and landed on https://www-jstor-org.byu.idm.oclc.org/ ('JSTOR Home') with NO login prompt. The EZproxy session is live in the personal profile. The public /databases/ index does NOT prove this -- it is unauthenticated; only a proxied resource does.

resolver.note: Every database on the A-Z list links through this resolver, which 302s to the EZproxy host. Slugs come from https://lib.byu.edu/databases/?letter=<a-z>. Examples: jstor, jstor-daily, jstor-plants.

ezproxy.note: OCLC EZproxy host rewriting. A proxied URL can be built DIRECTLY from a publisher URL without going through the resolver -- replace the dots in the hostname with dashes and append .byu.idm.oclc.org. Keeps the path intact.

library.gotcha: javascript_tool is PERMISSION DENIED on *.byu.idm.oclc.org ('Permission denied for JavaScript execution on this domain'). get_page_text, navigate and tabs_context_mcp all work there. Read proxied pages with get_page_text, not JS.

snorkel.note: Snorkel platform. Same profile as library.

fleming.note: micro1 primary. For library work: select_browser <personal deviceId>, then chrome-pin.sh restore when done -- select_browser clobbers the global pin.
